doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Giving notice to Hampton after eighteen years
summary: He told Hampton at the Port Authority he was quitting to follow his wife's wish; Hampton laughed it off and pressured him for months.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: No. Well I’ll tell you, I worked with that man 18 years, 18 long God damn days man, or years, I worked with him. And I remember we came from overseas, we had been on a trip like Germany, Switzerland, I can’t remember some of the other places right now. But anyway, we came back and I think we were coming to the Port Authority, so he was walking with his wife, and I walked up there and I said, “Hamp,” I said, “Listen man, I’m putting my notice in.” And he said, “Aw, Gates” he said. And he laughed, ha, ha. He said, “Man I’ll call you tomorrow, we’ll talk tomorrow. And he laughed it off. I said no, I’m telling you, I’m serious. I said my wife wants me to come in. She wants me to get work within the city. Because I’ve been out — most of my life we’re on the road. Sometimes I’d go out, and we’d stay out three months. You know? So he said, “Man, Zeke, come on.” He said, “No, don’t break up the group. Don’t break up the group.” I said, “Hamp I’m sorry, I’ve got to follow my wife. It’s her feeling, she wants me to come in and give it up, traveling. And so that was that. But that man, he browbeat me man for months.
